gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named tester's measured recording load for a four-camera unit under $300: EricSan on DashCamTalk measured the Vantrue N5S at 21.69 GB per hour with all four cameras at highest resolution (about 6 hours on a 128 GB card, about 23 hours on 512 GB).
standout_why: Compared against the two results I could read. Our own page (dealectric.com/best-4-channel-dash-cam, rank 1) already carries The Smart Home Hookup's Rexing R4-RD parking figure (0.4 Wh in 30 minutes), Vortex Radar's G980H findings and a calculated 20.7 GB/hour for the REDTIGER F17 Plus, so this angle is partly covered. Dashlore's guide has only maker specs for the N5S (60°C rating) and no measurement. Neither has a measured storage rate for the N5S or the Vantrue N5's measured parking draw and 11-second wake gap. The Tom's Guide roundup (rank 2) returned only navigation text, so I could not compare against it, and I did not open the remaining roundup results. I found no named measurement for the Rexing R4, Rexing C4 or REDTIGER VisionPano 40.
decides: It confirms the pick and does not change it. The only candidates with named measurements are the Vantrue N5S, Vantrue N5, Rexing R4-RD and Botslab G980H. The two exterior-side cameras ChatGPT favoured both drew negative named verdicts: The Smart Home Hookup called the R4-RD's daytime image its least favourite and its night plate capture 'just a blurry mess', and Vortex Radar said the G980H front camera 'really struggles at night'. The N5S storage figure adds card-size advice: about 6 hours of four-camera driving on 128 GB. The Vantrue N5 figures add a parking trade-off: 0.19 W in collision-detection mode, but 11 seconds pass before it records after an impact.

findings.note: Vortex Radar also says the side cameras are 'adjustable and helpful for recording inside and outside the car' and their IR LEDs light the cabin at night. Largely on our page already.
